spans.quotation: We report our sustainability performance using internationally recognized reporting standards and continue to assess other emerging frameworks amid a changing market and regulatory landscape. Our reporting is guided by the industry standards set out by Ipieca, the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), and the International Financial Reporting Foundation (IFRS) which includes the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) standards and Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations. Our reporting also follows the API Template 2.0 for GHG Reporting, the AXPC ESG Metrics Framework and Template and takes guidance from evolving nature-related frameworks. The 2024 Sustainability Report covers data from January 1 to December 31, 2024.

Data does not include heritage Marathon Oil assets unless otherwise noted. The Global Warming Potential (GWP) values from the Fifth Assessment Report (AR5) of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) were adopted in 2024 to align with most reporting methodologies used in the regions we operate, and in alignment with the GHG Protocol. This adjustment applies exclusively to the metrics for the year 2024 presented in the performance tables, and to our 2016 baseline target year for GHG intensity, as is standard practice, to ensure consistency between base year and future target years. As a result of this adjustment, the company total gross operated GHG emissions changes for the baseline year 2016 have been revised from 26.8 to 27.4 million tonnes of CO2e. Similarly, the values for 2024 have been updated from 16.2 to 16.4 million tonnes of CO2e. Data is based on assets where we have operational control. Environmental data is represented as 100% ownership interest and aligned with financial reporting. To provide the most current and accurate data available, we update previously reported data for prior years as needed. Data is normalized using barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) from production operations, including gas plant liquid production of ethane, propane, butane and condensate and production from third-party gas not accounted for in production operations. For gas production, 6,000 standard cubic feet of gas is assumed to equal one BOE.

Our reporting is in accordance with the GRI Standards and references guidance and standards developed by Ipieca, ISSB IFRS S2 and SASB. LRQA Inc. provided independent limited assurance of the disclosures and the 2024 data for the metrics in the performance tables. The ConocoPhillips Internal Audit group, which reports to the Audit and Finance Committee, also provided limited assurance of the data included in the report.

note: criteria 1, 3, 4 — 3 of 5. Criterion 1 satisfied by specific restatement figures in Span 2 (page 79): GHG 2016 baseline revised from 26.8 to 27.4 million tonnes CO2e; 2024 figure revised from 16.2 to 16.4 million tonnes CO2e due to GWP AR4 to AR5 transition; BOE normalisation factor of 6,000 scf stated. Criterion 2 not satisfied: no named target with baseline and target year in F1 spans. Criterion 3 satisfied by cross-cutting methodology elements across Spans 1–3: operational control boundary (100% ownership interest for environmental data, page 79); GHG Protocol GWP AR5 alignment as the restatement basis; explicit restatement policy (update previously reported data for prior years as needed); BOE normalisation approach (6,000 scf = 1 BOE); six named reporting frameworks spanning all canonical concepts — GRI, Ipieca, ISSB IFRS S2, SASB, TCFD, API Template 2.0 (Spans 1 and 3). Criterion 4 satisfied by explicit reporting period boundary January 1 to December 31, 2024 (Span 1, page 9). Criterion 5 not satisfied: no multi-year methodology evolution trend in selected spans. assured = true: Span 3 (page 86) names LRQA Inc. as independent limited assurance provider for the 2024 data for the metrics in the performance tables — this is the cross-cutting assurance section and is correctly selected at the F1 level; for all other concepts assured = false because LRQA was not named within their concept-specific spans. Internal Audit group also named as a second assurance layer. Boundary note: the operational control boundary in Span 2 (footnote 6, page 79) is cross-cutting and belongs here; the same principle applied specifically to Scope 1 on page 23 is a concept-level M1 statement. Marathon Oil exclusion policy (Span 2, footnote 1) is a cross-cutting boundary statement affecting M1, M3, O1, O2, and O7 simultaneously — the primary home for this disclosure is F1. The GWP AR5 restatement is a methodology change affecting M1, O1, and O2 simultaneously, confirming F1 cross-cutting scope.
